I am very open, about everything. I don't go out of my way to bring it up, but I never avoid talking about it. In fact, I generally consider it a defining attribute; part of "facts about me" for people whom I'm getting to know. I see it as an asset as much as it is a burden. Well, maybe not quite as much...

As yet, I've never had a negative reaction to telling someone. There's a lot of intrigue, usually; and tons of misconceptions that I have to correct. Generally, the most common false impression is that moods change suddenly and without warning often throughout the day. I know it probably does for some- but I feel it's safe to say it is outside the normal range.

The only thing that sometimes bothers me is when people say something along the lines of "Well, you're taking medication, right?" or similar questions that involve a presumption that I ought to be taking them. I do take medication, and am happy to share that fact, but I think it's a bad mindset to think it's something compulsory. This is especially bad for people who know and I mention that I'm just having a down episode. The first question often is "are you still taking your medication?"

 

Also, does anyone have any particularly good or bad experiences after disclosing you are bipolar? I don't mean when you were just explaining to someone after having a bad episode, just sort of a general type thing; but you can share those stories, too :)
